newsitem.title: MEXICO: INTERVIEW - Camesa eyes higher '97 net.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Camesa eyes higher '97 net.

text.p: Grupo Industrial Camesa, Mexico's steel rope and rod maker and fluorspar miner, sees net pre-tax profits rising to $250 million pesos in 1997 up from the $200 million expected in 1996.
"Pre-tax profits will be higher than this year," Camesa CFO Jose Gonzalez Monroy told Reuters in an interview Thursday.
Gonzalez said the rise will come from extra sales in both the industrial and mining divisions -- from higher installed capacities and volumes mined -- and productivity.
In Camesa's industrial division, Gonzalez said computer-aided plant changes to reduce bottlenecks will lift steel product capacity to 100,000 tonnes from 80,000 tonnes currently.

Talks to go into joint investment projects for even more capacity were underway with clients looking for more steel product, especially general purpose steel rod, but that nothing had been decided, he said.
In the mining division, he said flourspar output was up this year to 420,000 tonnes mined from 370,000 tonnes in 1995, which itself was higher than the 226,000 tonnes in 1995.

Camesa, whose Compania Minera Las Cuevas unit operates the world's biggest fluorspar mine, plans to build a new impurity removing plant next year. Fluorspar is a mineral used in the production of hydrochloric acid, aluminium and steel
"Tenders will go out in February for the contract," he said. He envisaged construction of the $15-20 million plant will take 12 months and will start up in 1998.

Gonzalez said the purifying plant idea was to open up more market opportunities and also to raise sales prices for fluorspar. He said impure fluorspar averages around $90 per tonnes compared to $120 for pure product.
"The payback is very solid," he said commenting on the planned investment.

Gonzalez said 1997 looked like a strong year for fluorspar exports, highlighting that contract sales to Japan already were set to rise to 75,000 tonnes from 60,000 tonnes this year. He said they could be even higher.

He shrugged off questions about competition from the world's other big fluorspar producer - China. "We have the advantage that shipments, usually leaving the port of Tampico, will always be more cost effective to U.S. and European markets coming from Mexico," he said.

Camesa was rescued from bankruptcy by banks in 1993. Banks Banamex, Bital and Banco del Atlantico took over majority control and still are at the helm of the company with a combined holding of 51 percent.
Gonzalez said he was not aware of any plans on the part of the controlling banks to sell their shares although he did not discount it could happen.
"It is my own personal opinion, but that (selling off shares) could be a very valid option," he said, declining to speculate further.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com))
